newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares hurdle 4,000 points in IBIS dealings.
newsitem.headline: German shares hurdle 4,000 points in IBIS dealings.

text.p: Germany's DAX index surged in late dealings to break the psychologically-important 4,000 point level as a firmer dollar and Wall Street gains gave the German market fresh energy as uncertainity evaporated.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings, ended up 56.62 points at 4,003.35 points and well above the bourse session when the DAX ended up 30.31 points at 3,972.84.
Dealers had earlier believed it was unlikely that a new record would be struck on Monday, but had said sentiment was generally good and further gains were likely.
But the market later gained momentum as the dollar turned higher after initially disappointing with a slight downtrend. The dollar was trading just above 1.7450 in early afternoon.
"The risk in the German share market at the moment is not to be invested in it," Susanne Schneemayer at Hypo-Research said in a market commentary.

"The status of our multi-factor model improved to show four rather than three positive indicators in the course of June," she said. "Such a status has in the past signaled a performance of 15-20 percent in the DAX over the upcoming 12 months."
A focal point in the market was ProSieben with shares listing in Frankfurt today. The issue, which was 50 times oversubscribed, was released at the top end of the subscription range of 72 marks.
ProSieben shares began trade at 87 marks and quickly jumped to the closing price of 95 marks. But even the close was below a grey market quote of 106.00 to 110.00 marks seen early this morning.
Retailer Metro was also a feature. Its shares jumped 9.40 marks to 205.50 on the back of news it was in talks to acquire the Makro cash and carry business from SHV Holdings.
